# Bring-up loop heartbeat jitter (generated by `python -m sw.loop_jitter`)

2026-11-27: 29986 heartbeat intervals over 60 s of `BringUp.cycle` at 500 Hz (joints pitch, roll, yaw, elbow, wpitch, supervisor in the loop, python-can virtual bus, drives answered by an in-process thread) on this machine (4 cores shared with other jobs, Linux 6.18.44-fc-v880, Python 3.13.18, load average after 0.58, 0.63, 0.40).

| Interval between heartbeat edges | ms |
|---|---|
| p50 | 1.99 |
| p99 | 2.25 |
| p999 | 2.75 |
| p9999 | 4.71 |
| max | 5.46 |
| mean | 2.00 |

| Intervals longer than | count |
|---|---|
| 3 ms | 15 |
| 4 ms | 7 |
| 6 ms | 0 |
| 8 ms | 0 |
| 10 ms | 0 |
| 15 ms | 0 |
| 20 ms | 0 |
| 25 ms | 0 |

**Loaded pass:** the same loop for 30 s (14949 intervals) with 3 busy-loop processes competing for the cores: p50 2.00, p99.99 6.72, max **7.89 ms**; intervals over 8 ms: 0, over 25 ms: 0; overruns 31.

Supervisor stops during the run: 0; loop overruns (a deadline missed by a whole period): 8.

**Use:** rnd/electrical.py sizes the A5 v2 watchdog monostable from this file (timeout ≥ the larger of 3 × the 99.99th percentile and 2 × the longest interval seen, rounded up to 5 ms, and the heartbeat-lost → no-torque chain ≤ the SW2 budget of 50 ms). **Caveat:** not the Pi 5 and no USB-CAN adapter. Re-run on the Pi before day 1 and raise the timeout if the longest interval there is longer; the safety step of sw/bringup.py also counts heartbeat gaps on the real bench.
